title: Stay Safe During a Windy Week in SoCal
summary: SCE crews are ready to respond as strong winds bring increased fire danger and the potential for Public Safety Power Shutoffs.
body_markdown:
If you haven’t secured the patio furniture yet, now is the time. Strong winds are heading across much of Southern California Edison’s service area and could stick around through Saturday.


The[National Weather Service](https://www.weather.gov/) has issued[high wind warnings](https://forecast.weather.gov/wwamap/wwatxtget.php?cwa=LOX&wwa=high%20wind%20warning) and[wind advisories](https://forecast.weather.gov/wwamap/wwatxtget.php?cwa=LOX&wwa=wind%20advisory) sweeping through parts of SoCal, with strong winds expected across portions of San Bernardino, Riverside, Los Angeles, Santa Barbara, Ventura, Kern, Tulare, Fresno and Madera counties. Sustained winds are forecast to reach speeds of 25-50 mph with gusts ranging from 50-70 mph. Isolated areas in the highest elevation ridgetops may see gusts as high as 100 mph.


[Red flag warnings](https://forecast.weather.gov/wwamap/wwatxtget.php?cwa=usa&wwa=Red%20Flag%20Warning) have also been issued for many of these same areas. Strong winds, dry vegetation and low humidity can create dangerous fire weather conditions. When the risk is high, SCE may temporarily turn off power in affected areas to reduce the chance of electrical equipment starting a wildfire. These[Public Safety Power Shutoffs](https://www.sce.com/outages-safety/outage-preparedness/outage-types/public-safety-power-shutoff-psps) are used to help keep customers and communities safe.


High winds can also knock trees and debris into power lines, causing unplanned outages. SCE crews are ready to respond and restore power as safely and quickly as possible.


Customers can check the[latest information about PSPS](https://www.sce.com/outages-safety/wildfire-safety/public-safety-power-shutoff/psps-weather-dashboard) and wind-related outages at[sce.com/outages](https://www.sce.com/outages-safety?from=/outages) .
